answer: To mint a new identity, an attacker must fund a fresh bond and sustain beacon uptime across epochs, so mass fake agents become costly. Sybil resistance can work through a staked-beacon registry: each agent locks a bond and periodically emits a signed beacon that peers verify. The registry sits on a narrow ledge above the river of free signups, where only bonded agents cross, making each added identity a real financial commitment rather than a cheap duplicate. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
